title: Cardinals, Panthers veterans report to camp on Wednesday
summary: The two teams will play in the Hall of Fame Game on August 6.
full_text: Training camp season is just about here. Veteran players from the Cardinals and Panthers are due to report to camp on Wednesday, which will make them the first two teams to have their full squads in place this summer. They have the earliest start date in the league because they will be taking part in the Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio on August 6. The Panthers will open up camp with right tackle Taylor Moton and cornerback Jaycee Horn on the non-football injury list. Moton is sidelined by a blood clot in his lung and the team expects him to play this season, but he is set to be out into the regular season. Horn is recovering from a cut on his foot and is due back much sooner. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett's status will be the big question once the Cardinals begin practicing. He did not practice during the spring while looking for a revised contract and has still not agreed to one, so his participation will be something to watch this week. The Seahawks and Patriots are next up on the reporting list. They will have their veterans in camp on Friday and all 32 teams will be ready to go on July 28.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks sign CB Brandon Johnson, cut TE Harrison Bryant
summary: The Seahawks made a change to their 90-player roster on the eve of training camp.
full_text: '' The Seahawks made a change to their 90-player roster on the eve of training camp. Seattle signed cornerback Brandon Johnson and cut tight end Harrison Bryant on Tuesday. Johnson signed with the Eagles as an undrafted rookie out of Oregon last year and played in three games as a rookie, spending most of the season on the Eagles' practice squad. The Eagles waived Johnson last month. Bryant signed with the Seahawks in April after spending last season with the Texans. He has previously spent time with the Eagles, Raiders and Browns. The Seahawks' rookies are already at camp and their veterans arrive on Friday. Their first training camp practice is Saturday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Pat McAfee addresses ESPN layoffs
summary: ESPN's clunky rollout of the latest round of layoffs, which included a long list of recognizable names, came at a time when ESPN is reportedly closing in on paying Pat McAfee $60 million per year.
full_text: '' ESPN's clunky rollout of the latest round of layoffs, which included a long list of recognizable names, came at a time when ESPN is reportedly closing in on paying Pat McAfee $60 million per year. That juxtaposition (triple word score) has created an obvious slew of what's-wrong-with-this-picture? complaints. McAfee addressed the pink-slip elephant in the room during his show on Tuesday. “ We hate any time this happens ," McAfee said, via Brendon Kleen of Awful Announcing . "Obviously this is terrible. We don’t like that. But we are very honored that we are still partnered with ESPN and Disney for the good of sport and the future.” McAfee nevertheless acknowledged the connection that is being made between ESPN not having the money to keep some employees while having more than enough cash to further break the bank for his weekday show and other assignments. “The first time we licensed the show through ESPN, one of these happened, we got blamed,” McAfee said. “OK, OK. Thank you. I feel like you don’t fully understand budgets and where things are coming from, but I do appreciate that. This time, we’re getting blamed as well. Which I guess I can understand, but I mean, there’s billions and billions of dollars in these companies, and hard decisions have to get made. And we don’t like any of them, and we hope we’re an asset to the company going forward.” Here's the basic reality at any company in any industry. The money is there for the people they want. For those they don't, certain opportunities arise (such as, in this case, the acquisition of NFL Network) to purge the ones they used to like but no longer do. It happens throughout American business. And it's driven by management. Currently, McAfee is one of the favorite sons in the eyes of those who have their hands on the wheel. And that's management's prerogative. The other reality is that management's prerogative can, and will, change. The only true job security is indispensability. For now, guys like McAfee and Stephen A. Smith have it. But the basic truth is that we're all replaceable. In time, we'll all be replaced. The only question is whether we walk away by choice, we're gently nudged, or we get a two-handed shove. The only protection against that comes from, to use the technical term, owning your own shit. McAfee owns his daily platform. If/when the ESPN run ends, he'll go elsewhere or he'll take the operation independent, again.
author: Mike Florio

title: Arizona Department of Gaming is investigating Cardinals' exec Ryan Gold
summary: Suspended director of college scouting facing another potential problem.
full_text: '' Cardinals director of college scouting Ryan Gold has two different problems arising from allegations of violating the NFL's gambling policy. First, Gold has been suspended indefinitely by the league. Second, via David Purdum of ESPN, the Arizona Department of Gaming is investigating the situation . A spokesperson for the Arizona Department of Gaming told Purdum that the department has been notified of the incident and "regularly work[s] with integrity monitoring organizations and sports leagues in situations like this." Gold is accused of making parlay wagers and sharing inside information regarding the team's draft picks. His lawyer, Mike Caspino, previously told ESPN that Gold's wife was making bets with a group of friends, and that Gold didn't know the team's draft picks before they were made. There has been some online chatter that Gold personally placed a wager on a parlay regarding the Cardinals' first five picks in the draft. That would be, even if Gold had full information as to the team's draft board, a difficult prediction to make because it takes only one team taking one player sooner than expected to send everything sideways. As we understand it, Gold is accused of sharing information about the team's intended first-round pick, running back Jeremiyah Love. Gold will say, we believe, that he didn't know Love would be the third overall pick, and that only owner Michael Bidwill and G.M. Monti Ossenfort knew. The league will say, we believe, that Gold's title and job duties put him in position to make a strong educated guess — especially since there were no surprises with the first and second overall picks. It creates a gray area regarding inside information. Gold possibly wasn't in position to know the exact truth, but he knew more than the average person by nature of his employment. As a source with another team explained it, the NFL wouldn't have made the accusation if they didn't believe they had the proof they needed. Really, why would the NFL shine a spotlight on what has become its first inside-information scandal in the age of legalized gambling if they weren't sure a violation had occurred. Gold nevertheless will appeal, and he should have a full and fair chance to defend himself.
author: Mike Florio

title: With camp looming, Buccaneers will "dive in" on Baker Mayfield negotiations
summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has set a deadline.
full_text: '' Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has set a deadline. His team is going to try to comply. Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated reported earlier this week that the Bucs are ready to " dive in " to negotiations with Mayfield, whose three-year, $100 million deal expires after the 2026 season. He's technically due to make $27.5 million this year, with available incentives. Past tinkering with his cash flow has pushed his total compensation for 2026 to $40 million. The most important figure is the cap number: $39.975 million. By rule, that pushes his 2027 franchise tag to at least $47.97 million, a 20-percent increase over the cap charge in the last year of the contract. The challenge continues to be pegging the right value, given that the range for veteran starting quarterbacks spans low in the $20 millions to the mid-$60 millions. The real question may be whether Mayfield's new-money APY begins with a "4" or a "5". The market is the market. But some teams (like the Dolphins in 2024) have done market-level deals they quickly came to regret. Whatever happens, bet on this — Mayfield will be willing to bet on himself, if necessary. During the latest season of Quarterback on Netflix, Mayfield revisits his decision to withdraw from Texas Tech after Kliff Kingsbury made Davis Webb the starter and enroll at Oklahoma without a spot on the football team. Mayfield has already made the ultimate roll of the dice on himself. And look at how it turned out — Heisman Trophy winner, No. 1 overall pick, and career earnings (through 2026) of more than $130 million. Mayfield's history makes it clear that he won't think twice about passing on a good-not-great offer from the Bucs and take his chances on something better if he becomes a free agent in March.
author: Mike Florio

title: New photo shows detailed Puka Nacua bite mark on woman who is suing him
summary: Rams receiver Puka Nacua's unusual 2026 began the night the year began, with a claim that he bit a woman on New Year's Eve.
full_text: ' Rams receiver Puka Nacua's unusual 2026 began the night the year began, with a claim that he bit a woman on New Year's Eve. On Tuesday, a more clear image of the alleged bite emerged. Madison Atiabi’s attorney, Joseph Kar, provided the photo to the California Pos t. It's a color version of a prior version of the same photo. And it shows imprints of roughly 16 teeth, top and bottom, in Atiabi's back. In March 2026, Nacua's attorney, Levi McCathern, dismissed the conduct as “horseplay” in comments to TMZ. Still, McCathern seemed to admit that at least one bite occurred, saying (as characterized by TMZ) that the bite left a “ temporary mark ." As compared to something permanent like a tattoo, sure it's temporary. But the image of it is clear and jarring. “I don’t know if you know,” Kar told the Post , “but the mouth is one of the dirtiest places on the planet given the amount of bacteria we have as humans. . . . My client has also suffered severe emotional distress and mental anguish and is being treated.” The civil case is ongoing. As also noted by the Post , Nacua may be eligible for a pre-trial diversion program in lieu of misdemeanor criminal charges. Entry into a diversion program would make Nacua susceptible to a suspension under the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Devon Witherspoon "further along" in contract talks than Christian Gonzalez
summary: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez wants a long-term deal, and the Patriots want to sign him to a long-term deal.
full_text: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez wants a long-term deal, and the Patriots want to sign him to a long-term deal. He shares an agent with Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, though, and Ian Rapoport reports that Witherspoon is "further along" in talks. The Seahawks have offered a deal that would pay Witherspoon "upwards of $30 million" annually, per Rapoport. That would make Witherspoon among the highest-paid cornerbacks in the league. Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie is at the top of the market at the position with an annual average of $31 million. Indianapolis' Sauce Gardner and Houston's Derek Stingley Jr. are at $30 million annually. Gonzalez, who is scheduled to make $2.259 million this season, won't be far behind Witherspoon in getting a new deal. The 17th overall pick in 2023 made second-team All-Pro in 2024 and the Pro Bowl in 2025. He has totaled 145 tackles, two interceptions, 24 pass breakups and a sack in three seasons.
author: Charean Williams

title: More than 62 million U.S. viewers watched 2026 World Cup final
summary: No USMNT?
full_text: '' No USMNT? No problem. Even with the U.S. team failing to make it beyond the Round of 16, the 2026 World Cup Final averaged more than 62 million viewers on U.S. television. Sunday's game between Spain and Argentina at MetLife Stadium, which Spain won 1-0 in extra time, averaged more than 62 million viewers between Fox and Telemundo/Peacock. The English-language broadcast on Fox averaged 38.937 million viewers. The Spanish version, on Telemundo and Peacock, averaged 23.9 million. It adds up to 62.837 million viewers. That's an enormous number, exceeding all NFL games for the 2025 season (including the regular-season record of 57.23 million for Chiefs-Cowboys on Thanksgiving) except the Super Bowl. It's also more than twice the viewership for the Miami-Indiana 2025 college football championship game, which attracted 30.1 million. What would the World Cup have done if the U.S. had somehow managed to make it to the last game? Surely, it would have been more than 100 million. And even though the World Cup is played only once every four years, no other sport (other than pro football) can touch those figures. Sorry, soccer haters, but the other football is absolutely a mainstream American sport — and possibly the most popular American sport other than the NFL.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Aaron Rodgers and family had been working toward reconciliation "for a while"
summary: It's very good news that Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has reconciled with his family.
full_text: '' It's very good news that Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has reconciled with his family. Family is everything. No one should be estranged from those who matter most to them. If/when walls are erected, it's important to find a way to tear them down. Ian O'Connor of The Athletic , who wrote a biography regarding Rodgers two years ago, reported that Rodgers and his family had been working towards a reconciliation " for a while ." Per O'Connor, Rodgers invited his parents, Ed and Darla, to his April 2026 induction to the Pleasant Valley High School Hall of Fame. Rodgers introduced his parents to the crowd, and he thanked them for their support. The reconciliation has its roots in Rodgers seeing, and hugging, his father at the American Century Championship in July 2023. Chronicled in O'Connor's book, it was their first contact in nearly nine years. It's a great development for the Rodgers family, and it's something that should inspire others who have grown distant from family to find a way back together. If you're in a situation like that, make the first move. Chances are that the family member with whom you've grown distant would welcome the opportunity to reconnect.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marcus Freeman is "all-in" on Notre Dame and doesn't see himself anywhere else
summary: Even as he turned down an opportunity to interview for NFL jobs this offseason, Marcus Freeman left the door open for an eventual move to the pros.
full_text: Even as he turned down an opportunity to interview for NFL jobs this offseason, Marcus Freeman left the door open for an eventual move to the pros. " Maybe sometime in the future , if it’s the right time and it’s what I think is right for me, then maybe I’ll pursue it," Freeman said in January. On Tuesday, Freeman made it sound as if South Bend is both his present and his future. “ I’m all-in . I’ve been all-in,” Notre Dame's fifth-year head coach told a small group of reporters, via Pete Sampson of TheAthletic.com. “I don’t see myself being the head coach or coaching anywhere else.” Freeman admitted in an Esquire magazine story this spring that a job coaching the Ravens or the Steelers would have intrigued him. Both jobs were open. He stayed anyway. “There were times when I wanted to listen to some other people and I did,” Freeman said. “It confirmed that this is the place I want to be.” NFL interest is unlikely to go away, no matter what Freeman says or how many times he says it. The question is: Will he eventually change his mind about leaving a premier college job for one at the highest level of the sport?
author: Charean Williams

title: Sam LaPorta fully cleared for training camp
summary: Lions tight end Sam LaPorta was fully cleared earlier this month, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
full_text: '' Lions tight end Sam LaPorta was fully cleared earlier this month, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports. The Pro Bowler is expected to be full go in training camp, though the Lions could be deliberate in his return. LaPorta played only nine games last season, with a back issue landing him on injured reserve in November. The herniated disc required surgery, but he went through walk-throughs during the offseason program. LaPorta finished 2025 with 40 receptions for 489 yards and three touchdowns. He had 86 receptions for 889 yards with 10 touchdowns as a rookie before tallying 60 receptions for 726 yards and seven touchdowns in 2024. He is entering the final year of his rookie deal as a second-round pick in 2023.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots put Harold Landry on the PUP list
summary: Patriots players began reporting to training camp on Tuesday and the team used the occasion to make a handful of roster moves.
full_text: ''' Patriots players began reporting to training camp on Tuesday and the team used the occasion to make a handful of roster moves. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that the Patriots placed edge rusher Harold Landry and tight end C.J. Dippre on the physically unable to perform list. Running back Terrell Jennings was placed on the non-football injury list. All three players continue to count against the 90-man roster limit and can be activated at any point during training camp. Landry dealt with a knee injury last season and did not take part in the team's practices this spring. Landry had 49 tackles, 8.5 sacks and a forced fumble last season. Jennings had 23 carries for 73 yards and a touchdown in seven 2025 games. Dippre appeared in two games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns sign CB Damarri Mathis
summary: The Browns made a change to their cornerback group before training camp gets underway next week.
full_text: '' The Browns made a change to their cornerback group before training camp gets underway next week. They announced the signing of Damarri Mathis to their active roster. They waived cornerback Dom Jones with a failed physical designation in a corresponding move. Mathis was a Broncos fourth-round pick in 2021 and spent three years with the team before being claimed off of waivers by the Panthers last August. Mathis tore his ACL a short time later, however, and missed the entire season. Mathis had 18 starts in his 43 appearances for the Broncos. He had 103 tackles, three tackles for loss and nine passes defensed in those games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Georgia RB Dante Dowdell seriously injured in ATV accident
summary: Georgia running back Dante Dowdell is being treated for serious injuries in an Atlanta hospital after an ATV accident, Bulldogs coach Kirby Smart told Mark Schlabach of ESPN on Tuesday.
full_text: '' Georgia running back Dante Dowdell is being treated for serious injuries in an Atlanta hospital after an ATV accident, Bulldogs coach Kirby Smart told Mark Schlabach of ESPN on Tuesday. Dowdell transferred to Georgia from Kentucky this offseason. He was injured near his home in Picayune, Mississippi, but details of the accident are unknown. "He's injured," Smart said. "We don't know when his return will be. I don't know the specifics of it, to be honest with you. It was a recreational vehicle, and he had some serious injuries." Smart told Schlabach that Dowdell is being treated at Shepherd Center, which specializes in treatment and rehabilitation, including spinal cord and brain injuries. "He's out of the really tough range, but as far as his complete health and coming all the way back, I don't know what that looks like in terms of this year," Smart said. Dowdell, who played at Oregon in 2023 and Nebraska in 2024, rushed for 560 yards and three touchdowns at Kentucky last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Recovering from torn ACL, Dolphins rookie WR Chris Bell placed on NFI list
summary: One of Miami’s rookies is not yet ready to participate in training camp, though it is not a surprise.
full_text: One of Miami’s rookies is not yet ready to participate in training camp, though it is not a surprise. The Dolphins announced on Tuesday that receiver Chris Bell has been placed on the active/non-football injury list. Bell, a third-round pick out of Louisville, suffered a torn ACL in November of last season. Because the injury occurred at the college level, he’s on NFI instead of the physically unable to perform list. Despite suffering the injury, Bell was still a first-team All-ACC honoree in 2025. While Miami’s rookies reported to training camp on Tuesday, the club’s veterans do not report until July 28.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Free agent DL Denico Autry is expected to retire
summary: Free agent defensive lineman Denico Autry is expected to retire, Aaron Wilson of KPRC reports.
full_text: ''' Free agent defensive lineman Denico Autry is expected to retire, Aaron Wilson of KPRC reports. Autry, 36, has not announced his intention yet. He became a free agent in March after his contract with the Texans expired. Autry entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent and played 12 seasons, four with the Raiders, three with the Colts, three with the Titans and two with the Texans. In his career, Autry totaled 331 tackles, 65.5 sacks, 117 quarterback hits, 35 passes defensed and eight forced fumbles.
author: Charean Williams

title: Netflix is expected to have Noah Eagle call play-by-play for 49ers-Rams in Australia
summary: Netflix is expected to have Noah Eagle on the play-by-play call for the second game of the 2026 NFL regular season.
full_text: Netflix is expected to have Noah Eagle on the play-by-play call for the second game of the 2026 NFL regular season. When the 49ers play the Rams in Australia, Eagle will be on the call , according to FrontOfficeSports.com. There's no word yet on who will join Eagle in the booth for commentary. Eagle and his father, Ian Eagle, both called play-by-play as part of the Netflix doubleheader broadcast last year on Christmas Day. Netflix also has a Christmas doubleheader this year (Bears-Packers and Broncos-Bills), plus a Packers-Rams game on Thanksgiving Eve and a Saturday Week 18 game with teams to be determined. The Rams are the designated home team for the Australia game, which kicks off at 8:35 p.m. ET on Thursday night, September 10, in the United States (Friday morning in Australia).
author: Michael David Smith

title: Panthers put CB Jaylon Guilbeau on NFI list
summary: The Panthers have added another player to their non-football injury list.
full_text: The Panthers have added another player to their non-football injury list. The team announced that cornerback Jaylon Guilbeau has been placed on the list. Guilbeau signed with the Panthers after going undrafted out of Texas in April. Guilbeau had 40 tackles, a tackle for loss and an interception in 12 games last season. Right tackle Taylor Moton and cornerback Jaycee Horn were placed on the NFI list earlier in the day. All three players can be activated at any point during training camp, but the Panthers said on Tuesday that Moton is expected to be out into the regular season. That will leave the Panthers even thinner at a key position as left tackle Ikem Ekwonu is still recovering from a torn patellar tendon.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Jacoby Brissett, Cardinals still have no resolution to contract dispute
summary: The Cardinals report to training camp on Wednesday.
full_text: The Cardinals report to training camp on Wednesday. Their biggest question is: Will quarterback Jacoby Brissett report, and if he does, will he practice or hold-in? Brissett has spent the offseason engaged in a contract dispute with the team, skipping the voluntary portion of the work. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that, on the eve of camp, the sides have come to no resolution. Brissett, who serves as his own agent, has negotiated with the Cardinals the past several months. The team acknowledges Brissett deserves a raise over the $4.88 million he's due to earn in 2026, per Rapoport, but the sides have yet to agree on the number. Brissett's deal has a max value of $5.39 million in this, the final year, but only $1.5 million is guaranteed. Brissett is the presumptive starter in new coach Mike LaFleur's offense, but the Cardinals also have Gardner Minshew II and rookie Carson Beck. Brissett started 12 games for the Cardinals last season, completing 64.9 percent of his passes for 3,366 yards with 23 touchdowns and eight interceptions. The Cardinals went 1-11 in his starts.
author: Charean Williams

title: ESPN ties layoffs to NFL Network acquisition
summary: One of my all-time favorite jokes (which may or may not be the untold "joke" from Big Shield) is a simple one that was told by David Letterman during a week of shows from Las Vegas in 1987.
full_text: '' One of my all-time favorite jokes (which may or may not be the untold "joke" from Big Shield ) is a simple one that was told by David Letterman during a week of shows from Las Vegas in 1987. It went like this. (And, yes, I found the episode on YouTube.) "Something really odd happened to me this morning," Letterman said. "I'm coming here to the hotel . . and I see this guy standing in front of the casino. Seemed like a nice enough guy. I don't know, like mid 30s or so. And he's kind of depressed, and he comes up to me, and he says, 'Excuse me, Mr. Letterman, can I borrow from you like $100?' He said, 'Because my wife is not well, and I need the $100 for some medicine, and hopefully, thank God, maybe she'll improve if we have the money to buy the medicine.' "I said, 'Geez, you know, of course I would love to help you out. But what guarantee do I have now, if I give you the 100 bucks, that you won't take it right there into the casino and spend it on gambling? Just blow it completely? Gamble it away?' "And the guy looks at me and he says, 'Oh, I got gambling money.'" ESPN, which has the money to pay many millions of dollars per year to select talent, is showing multiple other employees the door, based on money. And ESPN is specifically blaming the move on the decision to acquire NFL Network. ESPN poobah Jimmy Pitaro sent a memo to employees on Tuesday morning explaining the ongoing turmoil. “Over the past several months, we’ve made significant progress integrating the NFL assets that we acquired into ESPN,” Pitaro wrote, via Joe Reedy of the Associated Press. “Throughout this process, we have taken the time to carefully evaluate our collective teams, resources and organizational structure to best position us for the future. As a result, we had to make some difficult decisions about job impacts that we will be communicating today. “While most of the job impacts are tied to the acquisition, we will also notify colleagues in other parts of the company today that their positions have been impacted. We are committed to treating employees with compassion and respect and to providing support as they navigate this transition.” The "compassion and respect" portion of the memo didn't register with the in-house chatterboxes who shared information about several of the moves with the media. Which resulted in multiple employees finding out that they'd be former employees from outsiders, or (in the case of Ryan Clark) learning of their fate while on the air. It is, as previously mentioned, a crappy way to run a media company. Beyond the P.R. and H.R. misadventures that continue to unfold, the fact remains that, while ESPN doesn't have the money to pay a long list that includes more than a few long-time employees, it's got gambling money.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers to place CB Jaycee Horn, OT Taylor Moton on NFI list
summary: Carolina will not have two key veterans when they begin training camp.
full_text: Carolina will not have two key veterans when they begin training camp. The Panthers announced on Tuesday that cornerback Jaycee Horn and right tackle Taylor Moton will be placed on the non-football injury list. Horn is going on the list after suffering a cut on his foot that required stitches. Carolina is expecting Horn to return during the early portion of camp. Moton, however, is dealing with a blood clot in his lung. He was diagnosed with the condition in late June and was immediately placed on blood thinners. While the team notes he’s responding well to treatment, he is set to miss time during the regular season. Moton is expected to return at some point in 2026. The Panthers are also dealing with an injury to starting left tackle Ikem Ekwonu, who suffered a ruptured patellar tendon in Carolina’s postseason loss in January. The club signed veteran Rasheed Walker in free agency and selected Monroe Freeling in the first round of this year’s draft to improve depth at offensive tackle. Panthers rookies report to training camp on Tuesday, with veterans reporting on Wednesday this week.
author: Myles Simmons

title: John Harbaugh on Cam Skattebo backflip: "Dude, at least stick it"
summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo was tempting fate when he decided to do a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the weekend.
full_text: Giants running back Cam Skattebo was tempting fate when he decided to do a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the weekend. But his head coach didn’t see that action as too big of a deal, as he detailed in an interview with the Bleav in Giants podcast. “My reaction was — I haven’t talked to him yet, I’m going to talk to him I’m sure. My reaction was this: Dude, at least stick it . I mean, land the thing if you’re going to do it, you know?” Harbaugh said with a laugh. “That was my first reaction. “But Skat’s going to be ready to go. He’s been working super hard. He has really been training like crazy. And his mind is on camp. He’s healthy, he’s ready to roll, and I can’t wait to see him out there at practice.” Skattebo suffered a dislocated ankle midway through last season, but should be ready to make an impact on the field in his second season. Giants rookies report to training camp on Thursday, with veterans reporting on July 28.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cam Newton is laid off by ESPN, too
summary: The latest round of ESPN layoffs is impacting plenty of recognizable names — including a former NFL MVP.
full_text: '' The latest round of ESPN layoffs is impacting plenty of recognizable names — including a former NFL MVP. Via Bobby Burack of Outkick, ESPN has cut ties with former Panthers quarterback Cam Newton . Newton, who launched his own platform and showed that he has the chops to do the job, landed at First Take over the past two years as one of the folks appearing with Stephen A. Smith. Cam may have tiptoed on the third rail earlier this year, when interviewing Smith's sworn enemy, Jason Whitlock, on Newton's podcast. During the segment, Whitlock pushed the notion that Smith's memoir contains fabrications. Newton didn't push back. In every company, there's a political minefield that needs to be navigated in order to ensure long-term survival. Ryan Clark, for example, threw a low blow last September while on the air with a new employee who has close ties to ESPN executive vice president of programming and original content Burke Magnus. And that's the moment that reportedly caused ESPN to sour on Clark. The Whitlock interview may have caused Smith to sour on Newton. And with Newton's only role at ESPN being a member of the show Smith runs, that may have been enough to get Newton's name on the list.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jonathan Greenard: My job is to help Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt continue to grow
summary: The Eagles traded for veteran edge rusher Jonathan Greenard in April and signed him to a new four-year contract because they think he can make an impact for them on the field.
full_text: ' The Eagles traded for veteran edge rusher Jonathan Greenard in April and signed him to a new four-year contract because they think he can make an impact for them on the field. Greenard doesn't view that as the only reason why he's in Philadelphia, however. He will be part of a position group that also includes third-year player Jalyx Hunt and 2023 first-round pick Nolan Smith, and both of the younger players impressed him enough during the team's offseason workouts that he sees part of his role as making sure that they keep developing. "I'm really excited. Jalyx and Nolan, their game is only going to continue to grow ," Greenard said, via the team's website. "And I think my job here is just continue to help them with that. Any two cents I got, I'm going to [give them] to make sure that they get to that point that I know they want to get to." The best-case scenario for the Eagles would be for Greenard to remain an effective pass rusher while Hunt and Smith take the next steps to form a potent trio they can pair with defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis on the front line of the defense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tom Pelissero had a year left on his NFLN deal
summary: When ESPN acquired NFL Network, frayed nerves at NFLN were calmed by the news that ESPN would honor the existing contracts with on-air personnel, and that ESPN would make a decision when the current deals end.
full_text: '' When ESPN acquired NFL Network, frayed nerves at NFLN were calmed by the news that ESPN would honor the existing contracts with on-air personnel, and that ESPN would make a decision when the current deals end. Although the contracts may technically be honored financially, that doesn't mean the on-air NFL Network employees will continue to be on the air for NFL Network. As to NFLN reporter Tom Pelissero, multiple sources tell PFT that he had a year left on his contract. And while he'll surely be paid through the expiration of the deal, he'll essentially be sidelined until the deal expires. This means that the existence of an NFL Network contract won't be a protection against a potential layoff by ESPN, which is currently implementing a round of layoffs involving recognizable names and long-term employees. So, in addition to now assuming that being on the air won't be insurance against being laid off immediately, having an unexpired NFLN contract provides no protection against it, either.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ryan Clark takes the high road, after ESPN took the low road
summary: Clark responds with grace to Disney's Mickey Mouse move.
full_text: '' ESPN took the extremely ungracious step of informing NFL analyst Ryan Clark that he was being laid off while on the air . (At least it happened during a break.) Clark has opted to be far more gracious in his first public comment on the move. " Sending prayers and love to all those laid off today by ESPN," Clark tweeted. "So many of you have poured your life into that company, & I know how you’re feeling right now. My hope is as this door closes another opens for you all. God bless!" It really was a crappy, amateurish, Mickey Mouse move (which as to the last part technically is on brand). If, as has been reported, the goal was to prevent Clark from finding out about his fate from media reports, that's still better than telling him about it while he was ON THE AIR. Think about what that does to every ESPN employee who is on the air today, and for the foreseeable future. Logic suggests they won't do it again. But logic goes out the window when the mind wanders about the possibility that what happened to Clark will happen to them. At least one other person who has been targeted for layoff found out, we're told, from a member of the media and not from ESPN. This means that the S.S. Bristol is way too leaky. Someone who knows what's going to happen has been currying favor with media reporters by sharing information that should be kept confidential. Whoever is doing it is being a horrible teammate, and it is creating the impression that they're all playing for a horrible team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers' Taylor Moton diagnosed with blood clot in lung, will miss start of season
summary: The Panthers could turn to first-rounder Monroe Freeling to fill the vacant starting right tackle role
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers placed two veteran starters on the reserve/non-football injury list and announced that right tackle Taylor Moton and cornerback Jaycee Horn will miss at least the start of training camp as a result. Horn suffered a cut on his foot and is expected to return early in camp, while Moton's ailment is more serious. In late June, the 10-year veteran was diagnosed with a blood clot in one of his lungs.
Doctors immediately placed Moton on blood thinners. Daily assessments by the Panthers' medical staff determined that Moton is responding well to the treatment, but he will not be ready to join the lineup in Week 1. He is expected to play at some point this season, though it is not yet clear how much of the campaign he will miss.
A blood clot in the lung is a serious medical emergency that can be life-threatening. With treatment, the majority of patients make a full recovery, though some show long-term symptoms.
Moton has spent his entire decade-long career with the Panthers after they selected him in the second round of the 2017 NFL Draft . He played all 16 games as a rookie and has been an every-week starter at right tackle since the 2018 campaign.
The anticipated absence is a rare one for Moton, who played all of the Panthers' offensive snaps from 2018-23. He did not miss a single game until his age-30 season, in which he sat out three games due to knee and elbow injuries. He also sat out one game last year.
Having banked on Moton to anchor the right side of the offensive line, the Panthers will be forced to elevate a less-experienced option into the starting lineup until he returns. First-round pick Monroe Freeling is a candidate to jump into action right out of the gate. While he was projected as a still-developing lineman in the draft and appeared as a depth option during his practice reps earlier in the offseason, the Panthers may have no choice but to put Freeling in the mix.
Not only is Moton on the shelf indefinitely, but the Panthers are also awaiting the return of starting left tackle Ikem Ekwonu , who underwent surgery in January to repair a ruptured patellar tendon. Ekwonu is on the physically unable to perform list and looks like a candidate to miss extended time this season as he recovers from that serious knee injury.
If free agent addition Rasheed Walker fills one of the two vacant spots in the lineup -- most likely at left tackle -- then Freeling would become the next-obvious choice to step into the other role.
Freeling made just 17 career starts at Georgia and earned a second-team All-SEC selection during his third and final year of college football .
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL players' push for natural grass fields hits roadblock as league disputes injury concerns
summary: Raiders owner Mark Davis agrees with the NFLPA that NFL stadiums can support natural grass. The league says injury data doesn't favor grass over turf
full_text:
NFL players saw many of their stadiums swap artificial turf for natural grass when the venues hosted 2026 FIFA World Cup matches, and their collective reaction has grown into an NFL Players Association-sponsored movement. The athletes want the league to fully adopt natural grass and say that the World Cup proves it is feasible. Decision-makers, however, are split on the issue.
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle said this summer that he estimates 90% of players prefer to play on grass and that the league could fully adopt such surfaces if team owners "really gave a s---." Half of the NFL's stadiums already maintain grass fields, and one owner spoke strongly in support of them amid the players' call to action.
When Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis moved the team from Oakland, he only saw one option for the playing surface at his new stadium: natural grass. Davis showed that it is possible not only to grow and maintain a league-approved grass field in the desert but that it can also be done for an indoor stadium. The Arizona Cardinals have had a similar setup for two decades, too, with their retractable field tray.
"There was no way I was going to build the stadium or anything else to play on artificial turf," Davis said last weekend to the Las Vegas Review-Journal . "I just always felt that the safety issue, number one, and I grew up around football and the grass and mud and the smell of those uniforms after the game that you knew a football game was played. So, it was very important to me that we had grass."
Safety, as Davis noted, is the main reason why players so strongly prefer grass. When NFLPA executive director JC Tretter wrote his first argument for grass fields in 2020, he cited league injury data from 2012-18 that showed a 28% higher rate of non-contact lower extremity injuries on turf compared to grass. The data also highlighted that 32% more non-contact knee injuries and 69% more foot/ankle injuries occurred on turf during that seven-year span.
Players also note that turf places more force on the legs and that, anecdotally, they are more sore and require longer recovery time after playing and practicing on turf fields compared to grass surfaces.
The NFL has long held the stance that there is no meaningful difference between turf and grass with regard to injuries. The league pointed out two years, 2021 and 2025, wherein the injury rate across surfaces was nearly identical . NFL field director Nick Pappas made that same claim Tuesday in an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show.
"When we look across injury data, we no longer see this as an injury issue," Pappas said. "In the past, those concerns that turf was driving up the injury rate. When we look at the injury rate and the severity of injury -- and by that I mean the amount of ACLs, the amount of extended time-loss injuries, those real burdensome injuries -- when we look at that, it's a split, grass vs. turf. It becomes just the injury rate of playing football at this point."
"When we look at the injury rate and the severity of injury... it's a split, grass vs turf." – NFL field director @NPappas23 on the turf vs grass debate pic.twitter.com/ZCXKFyMods
While advances in turf technology have improved the surface's playability, the numbers the league points out in these arguments are cherry picked. The NFLPA unearthed more data in 2023 that showed the decrease in turf injuries and severity in 2021 was an outlier. Non-contact injuries occurred at a noticeably higher rate on turf in each of the nine prior years, and that rate rebounded again the year after.
The league's position is clear; it does not want to ditch artificial turf. The surface requires less maintenance and offers stadiums the ability to host a variety of non-football events with greater ease and, importantly, at a lower cost. Instead of swapping out the remaining 15 stadiums' fields (14 after Highmark Stadium reopens with natural grass), the league would prefer to push for innovation that makes turf more comfortable.
"From a surface hardness perspective, they're all within the same compliance," Pappas said. "What we're now chasing is how do we get that amount of energy lost to the surface or amount of energy gained back to the surface to feel more like grass? That's the target margin now, unless for some reason we can determine that there is an injury correlation to it. But that's what we hear the players say: They want it to feel more like grass. So that's what we're chasing now."
With the NFL and NFLPA standing on opposite sides of this issue and players' calls for full adoption of natural grass growing louder, this could become a sticking point in negotiations during the next collective bargaining cycle. The current CBA expires after the 2030 season.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Ranking the NFL's greatest farewell seasons as Aaron Rodgers looks to join an iconic list
summary: Rodgers says 2026 will be the final season of his Hall of Fame career. Before he takes his last snap, we ranked the greatest farewell campaigns in NFL history
full_text:
While the end of most playing careers is often sudden and surprising, there have been several instances where the end was either already announced or generally assumed. Aaron Rodgers put himself in the former category when he announced that the 2026 season will indeed be his last .
Rodgers has firsthand experience watching legendary quarterbacks end their careers. A 49ers fan growing up, Rodgers saw Joe Montana cap off his career with the Kansas City Chiefs following a legendary run in San Francisco. Five years later, Steve Young, Montana's successor in San Francisco, saw his career end abruptly when he was blindsided by a defender. In 2010, Rodgers then helped send Brett Favre into retirement by leading the Packers to a season sweep of the Vikings , his predecessor's fourth and final team.
This season, Rodgers will look to earn a spot on the following list ranking the best farewell seasons of the Super Bowl era.
Roethlisberger's 2021 season became an extended goodbye after reports surfaced before Week 13 that the Steelers ' longtime quarterback was entering the final stretch of his career. At that point, it was generally assumed that Big Ben was no longer in Pittsburgh's long-term plans amid the team's recent personnel and roster changes.
Roethlisberger's final season was a roller coaster. After a 1-3 start, the Steelers rallied to finish with a 9-7-1 record. Pittsburgh earned the AFC's final playoff spot after Roethlisberger led a game-winning drive against the rival Ravens in Baltimore. The Chiefs quickly ousted the Steelers from the playoffs, though, with Roethlisberger throwing for 215 yards and two touchdowns in his final game.
During his final season, Roethlisberger led the Steelers to season sweeps of divisional foes Baltimore and Cleveland. He remains the last starting quarterback to lead Pittsburgh to a win over the Browns in Cleveland. Fittingly, his last home game was a win against the Browns, one of the teams that passed on him in the 2004 NFL Draft . Throughout that game, Roethlisberger received cheers from Steelers fans who expressed their gratitude for his 18 seasons in the black and gold.
Brady briefly retired that offseason before deciding to play a 23rd and final season. Brady, 45 at the time, was coming off a brilliant 2021 season that saw him lead the NFL in pass attempts, completions, passing yards and touchdown passes. The general consensus was that the 2022 season would be Brady's last.
Simply put, the 2022 season didn't go as planned for Brady and the Bucs, who won the NFC South despite posting a losing record. It was the first and only time a Brady-led team finished below .500. Brady completed just 53% of his passes in his final game, a 31-14 loss to the Cowboys in the NFC wild card round.
While the season was largely a disappointment, Brady still put up impressive numbers, throwing for 4,694 yards and 25 touchdowns against nine interceptions while completing 66.8% of his passes.
Allen, who had announced during the offseason that the 1997 season would be his last, ran for 11 touchdowns during the final season of his Hall of Fame career. He also threw a pair of touchdown passes, including a game-winner against the Steelers on "Monday Night Football." Allen's play helped the Chiefs win the AFC West for the second time in three years.
In the playoffs, however, Allen and the Chiefs were upset by the eventual Super Bowl champion Broncos . Ironically, Allen's counterpart that day, Terrell Davis, had attended the same San Diego-area high school as Allen roughly a decade earlier. Three weeks after Denver's 14-10 upset win at Arrowhead Stadium, Davis led the Broncos to the AFC's first Super Bowl win since Allen's Raiders defeated Washington in the big game 14 years earlier.
The first defensive player to win league MVP, Page was released by the Vikings after failing to record a sack during the first games of the 1978 season. The 33-year-old Page was quickly claimed off waivers by the Bears and collected 11.5 sacks during the season's final 10 games. Page reunited in Chicago with legendary defensive coordinator Buddy Ryan.
After more than three seasons in Chicago, Page made it known that the 1981 season would be his last. He capped his career with a three-sack performance in a win over the Broncos that eliminated Denver from playoff contention. Page, 36 at the time, recorded 9.0 sacks during his farewell season.
Page's impact on the Bears lasted long after his final season. Late in the '81 season, Page wrote a letter to then-Bears owner George Halas on behalf of the entire Chicago defense asking him to keep Ryan as defensive coordinator for the 1982 season. Moved by the letter, Halas elected to retain Ryan after hiring Mike Ditka as his new coach. Four years later, both Ditka and Halas were carried off the field after helping the Bears win their first and only Super Bowl.
Reports surfaced in early December that Montana was planning to retire after the 1994 season. Despite playing in only 14 games, Montana threw for his most yards in a season since 1990, his second of consecutive MVP seasons. Montana went 9-5 as the Chiefs' starting quarterback during the regular season.
Montana's final season included a vintage performance in Denver on "Monday Night Football." After John Elway gave the Broncos the lead late in the game, Montana, who threw for 393 yards that night, responded by leading the Chiefs' offense on a 75-yard drive that culminated in his game-winning touchdown pass with 13 seconds left.
While he bested Elway that night, Montana's career ultimately ended in the first round of the playoffs against Dan Marino, another iconic quarterback who had fallen to Montana's 49ers a decade earlier in his only Super Bowl appearance. Montana played well in defeat , throwing for 314 yards and two touchdowns against one interception while completing 70.3% of his passes.
Instead of ending his career as Young's backup in San Francisco, Montana was able to step away from football on his own terms.
From a statistical standpoint, Barber had the best season of any player on this list. During his final campaign, Barber, who had made his retirement plans public that October, rushed for 1,662 yards while eclipsing 2,000 all-purpose yards for a third straight season. Barber also earned his third consecutive Pro Bowl selection.
In his final regular-season game, Barber ran for 234 yards and three touchdowns while helping the Giants clinch a playoff berth. Barber then ran for 137 yards in the Giants' loss to the Eagles in the NFC wild card round in what was his final NFL game.
Like fellow running back Barry Sanders had done several years earlier, Barber, who was 31 during his final season, also chose to leave the game while still playing at a high level. But while Sanders' decision did not cost him a spot in the Hall of Fame, Barber is still waiting for a gold jacket and a bronze bust in Canton, Ohio. The Giants' historic Super Bowl upset victory over the Patriots , which occurred a year after Barber's retirement, has probably contributed to his wait.
Before the start of the 2012 playoffs, reports surfaced that Lewis, who was returning from injury, had informed his teammates that he planned to retire after the season. Baltimore then went on a four-game run that culminated with Lewis hoisting the Vince Lombardi Trophy for a second time.
While a torn triceps sidelined him for most of the regular season, Lewis played and started in each of Baltimore's four playoff games. His 51 tackles and 29 solo stops led all postseason participants.
In his final game, Lewis had seven tackles while helping the Ravens edge the 49ers in Super Bowl XLVII. Baltimore's 34-31 win over San Francisco was also Ed Reed's final game in a Ravens uniform. Reed retired after spending parts of the 2013 season with the Texans and Jets .
Following Denver's thrilling AFC Championship Game win over New England, Manning was overheard telling Bill Belichick that "this might be my last rodeo,"…
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Aaron Rodgers reunites with family after decade-long estrangement: Inside the feud and how they reconciled
summary: The Steelers QB shared family photos on Instagram for the first time since joining the platform in 2023
full_text:
It's been an offseason of reunions for Aaron Rodgers , and his latest one came over the weekend when he reunited with his family.
The 42-year-old had been estranged from his family for more than a decade, but the ice started to thaw over the past few years, and it appears the relationship is now on the mend. The Steelers quarterback posted multiple photos of his family on social media Monday night. Rodgers has been on Instagram since 2017, and this is the first time he's shared a photo of anyone in his family.
Rodgers shared a total of five pictures on Instagram: One was with his mom (Darla), one was with his dad (Ed), one was with his brother (Luke), another showed Rodgers and his brother putting a toy together, and the final one showed Rodgers hanging out with his niece.
Rodgers added the caption, "Another bonding week."
It seems pretty clear that he wants his family involved in his life as he heads into what will almost certainly be his final NFL season.
In June, he made it clear the 2026 season would be his last dance .
"This is it," Rodgers said.
Rodgers will report to Steelers training camp on July 28 for the start of his 22nd NFL season.
It's not exactly clear what caused the feud between Rodgers and his family in 2014, but the conflict went public in 2016 after his brother, Jordan, appeared as a contestant on "The Bachelorette."
During one episode, Jordan brought the Bachelorette (JoJo Fletcher) home to meet his family, and the group ate dinner together. However, Rodgers wasn't there, and the family left two empty seats at the table to signify his absence (the other seat was for Olivia Munn, who was dating Rodgers at the time).
Rodgers kept quiet about the situation for more than eight years, but he finally gave his opinion on "The Bachelorette" episode in his 2024 Netflix documentary .
"I was quiet about it, because I thought the best way to do it was [to] not talk about it publicly," Rodgers said of the feud. "And what do they do? They go on a bullshit show and leave two empty chairs? They all agreed this was a good thing to do?"
Jordan and JoJo ended up getting married in 2022, but Aaron wasn't at the wedding. It's also worth noting that Jordan wasn't included in the photos released Monday night.
Another issue that seemed to divide the family was religion.
"I grew up in a very white, dogmatic church, and that just didn't really serve me. It was very rigid in structure. I'm not a rigid person. Shame, guilt, judgment," Rodgers said in the documentary . "It was like we have the truth, our way or the highway. Our way is heaven, your way is hell. Even talking to my parents, it was very black and white. Somebody has to be wrong, somebody has to be right. I kind of de-coupled from that in high school."
Rodgers has also dabbled in ayahuasca, something that didn't sit well with others in his life.
"When I started looking into other religions and plant medicine, I also found a lot of resistance," Rodgers said in the documentary. "Doing things, compared to what I grew up in, would be considered an alternative lifestyle. "
At one point in the 2024 documentary, Rodgers admitted a reunion with his family was possible, and now, two years later, that's finally happened.
Although Rodgers went almost a decade without speaking to his family starting in late 2014, the relationship with his family started to thaw after he was traded to the Jets in 2023. In a book by Ian O'Connor released in 2024 , Rodgers revealed that his dad decided to make the trip to Lake Tahoe in July 2023 to watch his son play in the American Century Championship golf tournament. Rodgers didn't know his dad was going to be there, but once he spotted him, he decided it was finally time to break the ice, and the two ended up spending some time together.
After that, things seemed to slowly improve. Both of Rodgers' parents were in attendance for his first game with the Jets , a painful one for the family during which Rodgers tore his Achilles in the first quarter.
It's not clear how much communication Rodgers has had with his family since then, but it looks like he's ready to include them in his life now. The next step for Rodgers could be introducing his family to his new wife. The Steelers quarterback secretly got married in a ceremony that took place at some point last year.
When Rodgers arrives at training camp next week, he'll also be in for another reunion. The four-time MVP will be playing under new Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, who also served as his head coach for 13 seasons in Green Bay.
author: John Breech

title: 50 days until the 2026 NFL season: Here are 50 under-the-radar players who could shape it
summary: From the big fellas up front to key pass-catchers, this list has it all
full_text:
The NFL is ever-changing. New coaches, new players, new rosters, new trends, new strengths, new weaknesses. The assertion that the league really stands for "Not For Long" isn't that far off. Teams rise and fall like the tides.
So, too, do players. While big-name trades, expensive free agents and the NFL Draft rule the offseason, much of a team's success can be attributed to internal improvement and finding the right supporting pieces. Hence, with 50 days until the 2026 season gets underway, we arrive at 50 under-the-radar players who could shape it.
This is the fourth year I've done this. You can see my 2023 , 2024 and 2025 versions, all of which had hits and misses. (It's a hard league to predict!)

title: NFL's most overrated and underrated quarterbacks entering 2026: Caleb Williams, Dak Prescott headline list
summary: Caleb Williams is the Madden NFL 27 cover star, but his inconsistency lands him among the league's most overrated quarterbacks entering 2026
full_text:
Quarterbacks make the football world go round. Every NFL season possesses quarterbacks that break out to ascend to new heights, like 2025 NFL MVP runner-up Drake Maye , as well as new lows like Minnesota Vikings 2024 10th overall pick J.J. McCarthy , a passer who ranked dead last in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) in 2025.
So, which quarterbacks' respective values are a little overinflated or underinflated entering 2026? Here is a look at some of the top selections for the most overrated and underrated quarterbacks, including the "Madden NFL 27" cover man.
Caleb Williams is the NFL's biggest rollercoaster passer. The highs can be incredibly high. He helped lead the Bears back from a franchise-record 18-point deficit in a 31-27 wild-card round win over the archrival Green Bay Packers , and he helped force overtime against the Los Angeles Rams in the divisional round with a miracle, fourth-down touchdown heave. Those miracle plays, and his 3,942 yards passing to set Chicago's single-season passing yards record, positioned him to be on the cover of "Madden NFL 27" this summer.
However, the high level of universal praise for Williams as the first Bears quarterback with a pulse since, perhaps, the pre-2010 NFC championship game Jay Cutler is a little much. The reason Chicago fell behind in both of their 2025 playoff games and lost in overtime to the Rams is because of Williams' inefficiency. He morphed into a turnover machine in the postseason, throwing two interceptions while completing just 24 of his 48 passes (50%) in the win against the Packers before throwing three more interceptions on 23 of 42 passing (54.8%) against Los Angeles. The third interception against the Rams came in overtime and doomed the Bears to defeat.
That extreme level of inefficiency in the postseason wasn't an outlier. He led the NFL in 2025 with 12 games possessing a completion percentage of 60% or lower, and no other quarterback registered a double-digit number of games in that category. Cam Ward was the closest with eight such games. The Bears' signal caller finished the 2025 regular season with a 58.1% completion percentage, the second-worst in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He finished ahead of only Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy and his 57.6% figure -- one that was so bad they brought in Arizona Cardinals castoff Kyler Murray to compete with their former 10th overall pick quarterback for the starting job. Williams' fundamentals still need plenty of polishing.
Williams' potential is tantalizing because he clearly possesses a high ceiling thanks to phenomenal arm talent and mobility. However, the hope and buzz about Williams currently outpace the reality of his latest on-field performance last season.
Bo Nix is an incredibly unique quarterback. He led the NFL with 612 passing attempts in 2025, but he failed to crack 4,000 yards passing, thanks to an average of 6.4 yards per attempt that ranked 28th among 33 qualified quarterbacks. That average was sandwiched in between washed versions of Aaron Rodgers (6.7 yards per pass attempt) and Kirk Cousins (also 6.4 yards per pass attempt).
Nix's inconsistencies helped produce sluggish victories against the Kansas City Chiefs ' third-string quarterback, Chris Oladokun , on Christmas in Week 17 (20-13), and a 19-3 home win over the Los Angeles Chargers ' backups. The young quarterback's lumps directly led to Denver struggling to consistently drive the football down the field. Three of the top four teams with the most punts in the 2025 regular season -- the Browns (93), Titans (78) and Raiders (74) -- missed the playoffs and fired their respective head coaches . The fourth team in that group is Nix's Broncos, with 75 punts. He benefits from a strong offensive line and a strong defense.
Add in the ankle injury, and it will be interesting to see what happens next in his career.
In Baker Mayfield's first two seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , he earned Pro Bowl nods while guiding his new franchise to back-to-back division titles. Mayfield undid all the growth from those two seasons in the second half of the 2025 season.
After throwing 12 touchdown passes to only one interception in a 5-1 start to 2025, Mayfield cratered across the final two-thirds of the year, tossing 14 touchdowns and 10 interceptions as the Buccaneers lost eight of their last 11 games to finish 8-9 and miss the playoffs completely. The end result of last season's campaign was Mayfield producing far and away his worst season of his three with the Buccaneers.
Entering the final year of his contract in 2026, it's now or never for Mayfield to prove he can still be a franchise quarterback. The last two years, plus his hot start to 2025, had people thinking Mayfield was an early MVP candidate, but now it's worth wondering whether he's running out of steam.
In his first year back from a season-ending, torn hamstring injury in 2025, Dak Prescott balled out. Despite the Dallas defense ranking as the NFL's worst scoring defense , Prescott played like a top-10 quarterback. He became just the ninth quarterback in NFL history to produce his third season with 4,500 yards passing. Prescott is now one of the NFL's best pre-snap quarterbacks, 10 seasons into his career, as his tape is littered with pre-snap adjustments that lead to big plays through the air.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
Prescott's reputation across the football world can sometimes be weighed down by the Cowboys of it all, thanks to owner/general manager Jerry Jones' struggles to build a balanced roster in the salary cap era, but Dallas' quarterback is one of the best in the league -- haters be damned.
There are only two quarterbacks with at least nine wins, 20-plus passing touchdowns and fewer than 12 interceptions in each of the last three seasons: Matthew Stafford and Jordan Love . Matt LaFleur's offense hums thanks to Love's deep ball accuracy and arm strength when squeezing the ball into tight windows over the middle of the field.
In the Packers' 31-27 playoff collapse against the Chicago Bears, Love threw for 329 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions while completing 73% of his passes (27 for 37). The narrative around Love entering 2026 would have been different had now- Brandon McManus not left seven points on the field in that game. That night, Love became just the sixth player in NFL history to throw for four touchdowns and no interceptions in a road playoff game. Had conservative game management from LaFleur and departed defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley, plus a total meltdown from McManus not occurred, Love's performance would be celebrated all offseason long.
Despite lackluster play from his offensive line for the vast majority of the 2025 season, Love more than made do with the offensive line protection he had to work with: Green Bay's offensive line allowed a quarterback pressure rate of 40.9% in 2025, the fourth-most in the NFL. A higher passing volume in the Packers' offense could also lead to a change in Love's perception. He attempted 439 passes, which ranked 19th in the NFL in 2025, but with an offense that is slightly more tilted toward the pass, this could give Love the opportunity to produce stats more in line with those of the league's more celebrated passers.

Trevor Lawrence initially struggled to pick up Liam Coen's offense, but once the lightbulb came on, he soared. He led the entire NFL in total touchdowns with 24 across the last eight games of the regular season, a span in which Jacksonville went a perfect 8-0 to finish 13-4 and win the AFC South. Lawrence's 38 total touchdowns ranked as the third-most in football last season behind only the league's last two MVP winners: Matthew Stafford (46) and Josh Allen (39).
Across the final six games of the 2025 season, Lawrence produced an absurd 19 total touchdowns to just one turnover. That feat…

title: MLB trade deadline buyers and sellers guide; handing out NBA offseason grades
summary: Plus, we have a new batch of WNBA Power Rankings
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The MLB trade deadline is quickly approaching, and the landscape has shifted a lot over the last couple weeks. Most notably, the Red Sox have gone from dead in the water to invincible. Go figure.
So, between the scorching hot Sox and a lot of league-wide mediocrity, our own Dayn Perry decided to sort through the trade deadline buyers and sellers . Boston -- which has now won 14 consecutive games -- has elevated itself into "likely buyer" territory as it looks to keep the magic rolling into October.
The Tigers land in the "Who knows?" tier, and that's fitting because there still isn't much clarity on the future of star pitcher Tarik Skubal . If Skubal does get moved, here are eight teams that could pull off the blockbuster trade .
One of the clubs looking to make a splash before the deadline passes on Aug. 3, the Braves , are reportedly pursuing a playoff-caliber starter to solidify their rotation for a World Series run.
With one very notable exception, the NBA offseason has started to enter a quiet period. As we await a decision from LeBron James , our own Sam Quinn broke out his red pen and graded each Eastern Conference team's moves to this point .
The 76ers are the star pupil this summer, acing every test to this point. The splashiest move, of course, was acquiring Jaylen Brown in a blockbuster move with the Celtics . That said, Philly also did exceptional work in the draft and free agency.
Not every team scored quite as well as the 76ers. Here's a quick look at the full report card :
The 76ers may not be done either, especially as they make their free agency pitch to LeBron. Philly has some competition there, however. The Heat are believed to be in the mix, and Pat Riley has been feeling a little nostalgic .
The only sports team hot enough to rival the Red Sox is probably the Valkyries . Golden State just rattled off nine straight wins to go from 10-7 to 19-7 -- good enough for second place in the league and first place in our WNBA Power Rankings .
Gabby Williams has given the Valkyries a major offensive boost -- averaging 15.1 points per game -- but the team's defense has been the real difference. Golden State is now at the top of just about every defensive metric the game of basketball has to offer.

title: Progress is paramount for the 2026 Falcons
summary: We’re not all that far away from the beginning of training camp, and I hope everyone’s enjoyed their quiet late spring and summer months. The Atlanta Falcons are going to be ramping up soon, and with that will come our own level of investment ramping up to heights that will be partially determined by just […]
full_text: Jun 16, 2026; Atlanta, GA, USA; Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski talks to the media before practice at Minicamp. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | Dale Zanine-Imagn Images We’re not all that far away from the beginning of training camp, and I hope everyone’s enjoyed their quiet late spring and summer months. The Atlanta Falcons are going to be ramping up soon, and with that will come our own level of investment ramping up to heights that will be partially determined by just how good this team looks in August. If I may try to frame up this season well before it begins, though, I’d say we should keep in mind that whether this year brings playoffs or seven wins, a Michael Penix Jr. renaissance or a Tua Tagovailoa spectacular, fantastic play or frustration, 2026 is about one word. Progress . The Falcons have been stuck in neutral for close to a decade now. They only truly bottomed out one year—that’d be 2020, when they started 0-5 and finished 4-12 while firing Dan Quinn and Thomas Dimitroff along the way—but have gone either 7-9, 8-8, or 8-9 in seven other seasons since they last pulled together a winning campaign. The roster has changed, the coaching staff has changed, the front office has changed, but what the Falcons have really excelled at since 2018 is milling about aimlessly. They never hit rock bottom, but they also never got particularly far off the ground over the course of all those campaigns. But as we look ahead, let’s not forget the way the last three regimes stagnated quickly. Dan Quinn and Thomas Dimitroff’s Falcons were great in his second season, good in his third, and mediocre-to-bad for three straight seasons. Arthur Smith and Terry Fontenot’s Falcons stayed mediocre after the team seemingly squeezed some real juice out of a depleted roster in 2021. Raheem Morris and Fontenot’s Falcons made splashy moves and ended up under .500 regardless. Those teams flickered dimly because the foundations they were built on poor decisions and shaky foundations, with stars who had to endure instability and incompetence just to drag this team to sevenish wins. This new regime will be justly judged not just on what they do year one, but what comes out of year one, and how sturdy the foundation and the strategy both seem to be and ultimately are. I don’t expect Kevin Stefanski, Ian Cunningham, and Matt Ryan to be miracle workers. I don’t think this team has the talent base, top to bottom, of a Super Bowl-contending team. I think competent quarterback play and competent coaching could have them pushing for a wild card slot or (unfortunately, a likely to be less impressive) NFC South title, especially given the deep uncertainty swirling around the division. But what I’m ultimately looking for is a sign that this franchise is moving away from the morass of mediocrity we Falcons fans have become used to and toward a future where Atlanta football matters again. I want signs the plan is working, that the pieces this new regime has put together show the brain trust will know what they’re doing with a full complement of draft picks in 2027 and plenty of cap space, and a sense that the young talent is developing instead of foundering. I want signs of thoughtful building, real talent, and a rudder for a ship that long ago forgot what it even meant to have a rudder. That could mean that a healthy Penix has improved footwork and accuracy that unlocks his potential, the kind of progress that sets the Falcons up to not have to fret about quarterback. It may mean that Jalon Walker goes from promising rookie to true star, or that rookies like Avieon Terrell hit the ground running and start in a defense teeming with young talent delivering on potential. It may mean Kyle Pitts is finally featured, that Jahan Dotson becomes the starting-caliber wide receiver his pre-draft promise indicated he could be, or that the Falcons stop burning timeouts at the worst time and taking dumb penalties when they are least welcome. It could mean that the moves to fill out the roster in August or to patch a hole opened by injury right after cuts are savvy instead of exciting and then ultimately disappointing. What we’re looking for is progress in all its facets, from performance to planning to development to dealing with adversity. For a team that has struggled off the field and on the field for years, every scrap of “these guys know what they’re doing” and “they just look better than Team X” will be water in a dry, dry desert. In the weeks ahead, we’ll have ample reason to focus on the position battles, the clawing to latch on to the roster, the buzzwords and scheming and shuffling that the coaching staff and front office will do, and we’ll be floating in the minutiae of this team the way we do every August. That’s immersion that gets us ready for the season ahead, and one of the wonders of being a fan is that we can and will get freshly invested in a young wide receiver who pops off for 100 yards in a Week 2 preseason game, or an undrafted quarterback making a push for a practice squad spot. It’s a beautiful thing, and late July and August are never the time to hold your favorite team at arm’s length. We’ll want to see progress in terms of what it means for this season, not the far-off future, and that could take many different forms from a stouter run defense to more consistent quarterback play to getting a healthy Bralen Trice on the field. What will matter is, of course, to be determined. From there, how that modest progress translates meaningfully onto the field for the regular season and into the way the team handles its remaining weaknesses with an eye on winning both this year and into the future will really matter. I won’t say the wins and losses don’t matter, because of course they do. We desperately want to see this team win, make a playoff push, and start swinging for glory again. But if this isn’t the year that brings the Falcons back to relevance and postseason success, may it deliver progress. May progress, in fact, be the theme of this team’s 2026 with such a pivotal, resource-rich 2027 en route, starting with what I hope is an encouraging and successful training camp and preseason in just a bit over a week.
